text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller was lying when she said in a speech on Saturday that the Sabah newspaper group had received $200 million from the state.
- Ankara state security court has started procedings against four MPs of the Islamist Welfare Party for "provoking hatred and enmity" during speeches made defending religious schooling.
- Ciller attacked the media, making a number factual errors during a speech at a rally of 6,000 supporters instead of the expected 100,000.
- Turkish white goods manufacturer, Beko, made $80 billion worth of exports to Britain in 1996.
- Left-wing party leader, Bulent Ecevit, said that ideological differences stop his party uniting with the other major leftist party, not personal differences with its leader, Deniz Baykal.
- A village imam has been appointed manager of a state hospital by the Islamist minister of public works.
- The Islamic businesmen's association, MUSIAD, is encouraging its members to go into weapons manufacturing.
- Villagers protesting against a proposed gold mine to be built by Eurogold, set up a road block, stopping State Minister Riza Guneri who was visiting the site.

- Tension between the government and the secularist press is rising as Ciller accuses the major media groups of taking billions of dollars in state aide and justice minister, Sevket Kazan opens proceding against certain secularist journalists.
